title.rendered: iOS History: Every Version From iPhone OS 1 to iOS 26 Explained

content.rendered:
Since its debut in 2007 alongside the first iPhone, iOS has come a long way. Each new version has brought fresh features, design changes, and performance improvements. iPhone OS 2 brought the App Store, while iOS 14 incorporated 5G connectivity, iOS 18 introduced Apple Intelligence features, and iOS 26 offered a new Liquid Glass design.

In this editorial, we will revisit history and discuss different versions of iOS, from the initial iPhone OS to the recently launched iOS 26. You will learn about the key updates of various versions and the turning points in the evolution of the iOS operating system.

Table of Contents
  • iOS 26 (2025)
  • iOS 18 – September 16, 2024
  • iOS 17 – September 18, 2023
  • iOS 16 – September 12, 2022
  • iOS 15 – September 24, 2021
  • iOS 14 – September 17, 2020
  • iOS 13 – September 19, 2019
  • iOS 12 – September 17, 2018
  • iOS 11 – September 19, 2017
  • iOS 10 – September 13, 2016
  • iOS 9 – September 16, 2015
  • iOS 8 – September 17, 2014
  • iOS 7 – September 18, 2013
  • iOS 6 – September 19, 2012
  • iOS 5 – October 12, 2011
  • iOS 4 – June 22, 2010
  • iPhone OS 3 (iOS 3) – June 17, 2009
  • iPhone OS 2 (iOS 2) – July 11, 2008
  • iPhone OS 1 (iOS 1) – June 29, 2007

iOS 26 (2025)

Apple unveiled iOS 26 during WWDC 2025 on June 9, marking a significant shift in the iPhone’s software journey. It introduced a bold redesign and a new naming convention—aligning the version number with the calendar year of intended use (2026). This change brought uniformity across all Apple platforms, including macOS, iPadOS, watchOS, and tvOS.

The standout feature of iOS 26 is the Liquid Glass design language, inspired by visionOS. This aesthetic replaces the long-standing flat design introduced in iOS 7 with translucent, curved, and refractive UI elements that feel more fluid and immersive. Apps like Camera, Photos, Messages, and Phone received major interface upgrades, creating a more cohesive user experience.

Apple also supercharged its Apple Intelligence suite. With improvements to Visual Intelligence, Image Playground, and Shortcuts, iOS 26 introduced new capabilities like Live Translation, Call Screening, and DJ-style Audio Mix. Even CarPlay saw enhancements, with support for Live Activities and Tapbacks.

Apple released the developer beta of iOS 26 on June 9, 2025, followed by the public beta in July. The full version rolled out in September alongside the launch of the iPhone 17 series.

Key Features of iOS 26

  • A striking new Liquid Glass design language featuring translucent, refractive UI elements—widgets, icons, controls.
  • The clock resizes based on Lock Screen wallpaper subjects and the notification stack.
  • 3D Spatial Scene wallpapers make images pop when tilted.
  • Live Translation offers real‑time language translation in Messages, FaceTime, and Phone calls.
  • Visual Intelligence analyzes screenshots or on-screen content to search for objects or text, allowing for interaction across multiple apps.
  • Genmoji lets you create personalized emojis by combining existing ones.
  • Image Playground received a new ChatGPT-style for image creation.
  • Shortcuts include Apple Intelligence tools in workflows.
  • AI auto‑suggest reminders from messages/emails.
  • Adaptive Power Mode saves battery when usage peaks, without entering Low Power Mode.
  • The Lock Screen displays charging time estimates; battery settings provide color-coded usage statistics.
  • Call Screening asks for the caller’s identity and intent.
  • Hold Assist automatically waits on hold during phone calls until a real person answers.
  • The Messages app now features real-time typing indicators, built-in poll creation in group chats, custom backgrounds, and spam-sorting filters.
  • Safari in iOS 26 received a compact layout style, web app support for all websites, and improved link tracking protection.
  • The new Games app organizes recently played titles and provides personalized recommendations.
  • The Music app gets a live radio widget, DJ-Style AutoMix, and Lyric Translations.
  • The Photos app introduced separate Library and Collections tabs, as well as support for 3D spatial photos.
  • Apple Maps in iOS 26 included tracking preferred routes and Visited Places.
  • Use AirPods to control iPhone camera—press or hold to snap a photo or start a video.
  • CarPlay now features a compact call view, Tapbacks, and pinned conversations in Messages.
  • Digital U.S. Passport support in Wallet.
  • Recovery Assistant introduced restoration using another iPhone or iPad.
  • You can now set custom snooze durations in the Alarm app.

iOS 18 – September 16, 2024

Apple gave iPhone users a preview of iOS 18 at WWDC 2024 and officially launched it on September 16, 2024, along with the iPhone 16 series. This major update significantly boosts personalization options across the system and apps. You can customize the Home Screen layout and change the app icon theme.

Additionally, the Control Center can be customized to accommodate new quick controls. For advanced privacy, iOS 18 allows users to lock apps and select which apps can access specific contacts.

The native apps, especially the Photos, Notes, and Mail apps, also received a major overhaul. Further, the company introduced a powerful AI-powered feature called Apple Intelligence. Last but not least, the iOS 18 Accessibility features make it easier to navigate the iPhone.

Key features of iOS 18

  • Apple Intelligence features such as Genmoji, Math Notes, etc.
  • Call recording
  • Customizable Home Screen
  • Redesigned Control Center
  • New controls on the Lock Screen
  • Lock and hide apps
  • A new Passwords app
  • Collections and Clean Up tool in the Photos app
  • iPhone Game mode
  • Text effects in Messages
  • New emojis in Tapback
  • Schedule messages with Send Later
  • Messages via Satellite
  • Categories in the Mail app
  • Highlights in Safari
  • Redesigned Reader in Safari
  • Calculator history
  • Download topographic maps
  • Tap to Cash in the Wallet app
  • Live audio transcription in Notes
  • Integrated Reminders in Calendar
  • Enhanced Journal app

iOS 17 – September 18, 2023

iOS 17 was announced at WWDC 2023. The focus of iOS 17 was on redesigning and upgrading the system apps and features. The Message, FaceTime, and Phone apps have several enhancements. Additionally, Apple enhanced connectivity by introducing NameDrop and FaceTime on Apple TV.

The most highlighted features of iOS 17:

  • Personalized Contact Posters 
  • Live Voicemail 
  • Video voicemail and Reactions on FaceTime 
  • Search Filter, Catch up arrow, Swipe to reply, Transcription of voice messages, Check-in features in the Messages app
  • Live Stickers 
  • StandBy feature 
  • Share a contact card using NameDrop 
  • Journal app
  • The mindfulness feature on the Health app
  • Create Profiles on Safari 
  • Collaborated playlist on CarPlay
  • Upgraded Autocorrect and Dictation abilities 

iOS 16 – September 12, 2022

iOS 16 was announced at the WWDC event in June 2022 and released in September 2022.

The most noticeable upgrade in iOS 16 was the addition of supported features for the Dynamic Island on iPhone 14 Pro models. It made the new notch design more fun by displaying animated notifications and offering controls around the camera. 

Also, Crash Detection, Always-on display, Emergency SOS via Satellite, and other exclusive features of the iPhone 14 series are supported with iOS 16. 

Key features of iOS 16:

  • Customizable Lock Screen
  • Live Activities
  • Better Focus Filters
  • New Message features
  • Redesigned Apple Maps
  • Apple Pay Later
  • Apple Order Tracking
  • iCloud Shared Photo Library
  • Live Texts on videos
  • Passkeys
  • Safety Check function
  • Improvements to Spatial Audio
  • Voice Isolation in phone calls
  • Advanced Data Protection for iCloud
  • Apple Music Sing karaoke

iOS 15 – September 24, 2021

Unlike iOS 16, the iOS 15 update focused more on software bug fixes, system improvements, and refining the features of built-in apps.

Additionally, the pandemic era influenced the introduction of these feature upgrades. Apple focused on enhancing security and privacy, preventing ad tracking, and improving Siri, Camera, FaceTime, Messages, and other features. 

As of writing, iOS 15 is supported on the iPhone 6S series and later, as well as the iPod touch 7th generation.  

Key features of iOS 15:

  • New FaceTime features – Spatial audio, SharePlay, FaceTime Link, Mic modes, Portrait modes, etc.
  • iMessage Share with you 
  • Better Focus Filters with Notification Summary, Signal your status, etc.
  • Live Text and Memory features in the Photos app
  • Advanced Spotlight search
  • App Privacy Report
  • Mail Privacy Protection
  • On-device Siri
  • Digital Legacy program
  • Redesigned Safari tabs
  • Detailed Maps  
  • Improved Health and Wallet app

iOS 14 – September 17, 2020

The iOS 14 version lists similar system improvements, very much like iOS 15. There were no significant changes. Apple added several enhancements, including privacy controls, Home Screen widgets, and customization options. 

Key features of iOS 14:

  • Widgets on the Home Screen
  • App Library
  • Improved call notifications
  • Picture in Picture Mode
  • Redesigned Siri 
  • Translation, Password monitoring, and Website Privacy Report in Safari
  • Pinned Conversations and improved group texting in Messages
  • New Memoji Styles and Stickers
  • Cycling directions and Electric vehicle routing in Maps
  • Translate app
  • App Clips

iOS 13 – September 19, 2019

Before iOS 13, iPad also ran iOS. However, Apple took a significant step by introducing a new iPadOS, designed to make the iPad more productive and potentially serve as a laptop replacement. Since then, iOS and iPad OS have always been rolled out simultaneously.

The most noticeable new feature was the introduction of Dark Mode. Additionally, iOS 13 improved essential functions, such as faster app start-up, Face ID, Portrait Lighting, and the redesign of pre-installed apps.

Key features of iOS 13: 

  • System-wide Dark Mode
  • 30% faster Face ID unlocking
  • Revamped Apple Maps
  • Smarter HomeKit
  • Sign In With your Apple user account
  • New privacy and security options
  • Portrait Lighting Effects
  • New, improved Siri voice
  • Overhauled system apps like Photos, Mail, Reminders, and Notes

iOS 12 – September 17, 2018

The 12th iteration of the iPhone software had just a few new additions. Primarily, it improved regularly used functionality for providing a better user experience. Apple introduced Siri Shortcuts, ARKit 2, Screen Time tracking, etc.

Key features of iOS 12:

  • Grouped Notifications
  • Screen Time
  • ARKit 2 for enhanced Augmented Reality
  • Siri improvements
  • Memoji

iOS 11 – September 19, 2017

iOS 11 has special features to support the iPod touch, iPad, Apple Watch, and Apple TV.

Therefore, its primary features included more iPad-specific features, such as split-screen apps, drag-and-drop functionality, a file browser app, and support for Apple Pencil handwriting. 

Key features of iOS 11:

  • iPad functions
  • AirPlay 2 
  • Support for Augmented Reality

iOS 10 – September 13, 2016

The release of iOS 10 was a watershed moment for the Apple ecosystem. It offered several APIs to integrate third-party solutions into the system apps. Thus, the iPhone gained a boost in interoperability and customization through its UI and applications. Additionally, Siri has become more accessible to third-party apps. The best part was that Apple allowed users to uninstall built-in apps.

Key features of iOS 10:

  • Embedded ​iMessage apps
  • Delete built-in apps
  • Split Control Center into multiple panels
  • Integration of Siri with third-party apps
  • Smarter QuickType keyboard
  • 3D Touch displayed widgets 

iOS 9 – September 16, 2015

iOS 9 prioritized building a solid base for the operating system to improve the speed, responsiveness, stability, and performance of older devices. After significant modifications to iOS’s design and technological base, users started to feel that iOS was no longer the reliable, trustworthy, and competent it had previously been. 

So, Apple decided to focus on strengthening the OS’s foundation rather than introducing new features, laying the groundwork for the larger enhancements in the next iOS updates. To garner public reaction and acceptance, iOS introduced the Public Beta feature. So, before the actual release of the upcoming iOS version update, people can get a taste of it.

Key features of iOS 9:

  • Night Shift
  • Low Power Mode
  • Public beta program

iOS 8 – September 17, 2014

In iOS history, iOS 8 was a significant update as it introduced the contactless payment system Apple Pay and the Apple Music subscription service. It also polished the iCloud features for more reliable and consistent performance. The most useful feature unveiled was the Handoff feature, which allows for seamless switching between Apple devices.

Apple walked in with a Dropbox-like iCloud Drive and the addition of an iCloud Picture Library and an iCloud Music Library. To save subscription costs, Apple offered Family Sharing, which allows users to enjoy content individually with a single subscription. Moreover, the HealthKit and HomeKit features focused on users’ daily lives.

Key features of iOS 8:

  • Apple Music
  • Apple Pay
  • iCloud Drive
  • Handoff
  • Family Sharing
  • Spotlight Suggestions
  • QuickType on keyboard
  • HomeKit and HealthKit
  • Extensibility framework for third-party extensions

iOS 7 – September 18, 2013

iOS 7 was a troublesome update, and users were dissatisfied as things didn’t operate as expected. The update included a significant redesign of the user interface, opting for a flat look. However, some users found it difficult to read due to the tiny, thin letters, and others experienced motion sickness from the constant animations. 

Additionally, Apple provided quick access to the most frequently used features through Control Center and introduced AirDrop, Activation Lock, and CarPlay. Additionally, Siri got new voices and a redesigned look.

Key features of iOS 8:

  • Activation Lock
  • AirDrop
  • CarPlay
  • Control Center
  • Thumbnails in App Switcher
  • Improved Notification Center
  • Smarter Siri
  • Touch ID

iOS 6 – September 19, 2012

In the history of iOS versions, iOS 6 saw the most controversy due to Apple’s escalating rivalry with Google. Although the newly launched Siri was a significant breakthrough in technology, issues with it led to substantial revisions.

Besides, from iPhone OS version 1.0, Google has included the Maps and YouTube applications pre-installed. But this time, Apple replaced Google Maps with a new Apple Maps. It fell short due to glitches, inaccurate instructions, and issues with other functionalities. 

Sidelining the flaws, iOS 6 features a Podcast app, a more capable Siri, a Panoramic mode in the Camera, and the ability to make FaceTime calls over cellular data.

Key features of iOS 6:

  • Apple Maps
  • Do Not Disturb
  • Passbook (now Wallet)
  • New features in Siri, like launching apps
  • Panoramic photos
  • FaceTime over cellular data

iOS 5 – October 12, 2011

iOS 5 was a turning point for Apple, as it introduced crucial new features, including Siri, iCloud, wireless iPhone activation, and Wi-Fi iTunes syncing. Users could download and install software updates on their iPhones without a computer. Additionally, for a better user experience and accessibility, the iPhone features Notification Center and iMessage.

Key features of iOS 5:

  • Siri
  • iCloud
  • iMessage
  • Notification Center
  • Redesigned Reminders and Newsstand apps
  • Wireless syncing and activation

iOS 4 – June 22, 2010

With iOS 4, the futuristic iOS began to take form as Apple renamed the “iPhone OS” to “iOS” for the first time. Many revisions to this version included features such as FaceTime, multitasking, iBooks, Game Center, organizing programs into folders, custom wallpapers, Personal Hotspot, AirPlay, and AirPrint.

Moreover, Apple included Bing as a search engine for Safari and enabled users to consolidate multiple email accounts into a single inbox. It was the first iteration of iOS to stop supporting all iOS devices. It was incompatible with the first-generation iPod touch or the iPhone.

Key features of iOS 4:

  • FaceTime
  • Multitasking
  • AirPlay
  • AirPrint
  • iBooks
  • Game Center
  • Personal Hotspot
  • System-wide spell checking
  • 5x digital zoom

iPhone OS 3 (iOS 3) – June 17, 2009

iOS 3 was the first operating system for the iPad and came pre-installed on the iPhone 3GS without any additional charge. Users could copy and paste text system-wide. Besides, Spotlight search, MMS support in the Messages app, and the capability to shoot films using the Camera app are just a few of the new features it includes.

Key features of iOS 3;

  • Copy and paste​
  • Spotlight​ search​
  • Voice Memo app
  • Recording videos

iPhone OS 2 (iOS 2) – July 11, 2008

iPhone OS 2 was meant for the iPhone 3G model, which included support for the 3G network. As the iPhone became a huge hit, app developers attempted to jailbreak it to install third-party apps. So, Apple introduced development tools like APIs and SDKs for software companies to launch apps in the App Store, thereby preventing the installation of apps from the web.

The App Store had around 500 applications when it debuted. Podcast support, walking and public transportation instructions in Maps, an iTunes Genuine playlist, and enhancements to Mail, Calculator, and Contacts using Microsoft Exchange support were other significant additions to iPhone OS 2.

Key features of iOS 2:

  • App Store​
  • Developer APIs and SDKs
  • Support for Microsoft ActiveSync and Microsoft Exchange
  • Improved Maps app​

iPhone OS 1 (iOS 1) – June 29, 2007

iOS debuted with the release of the first iPhone in June 2007. Nevertheless, it was mostly powered by OS X, the Mac software. It featured a core iOS UI, iTunes integration, Multi-touch gestures, Mobile Safari, iPod, Visual Voicemail, and Maps, which were advanced smartphone capabilities at the time.

However, it lacked support for third-party applications and came with basic pre-installed apps, including Calendar, Pictures, Camera, Notes, Mail, and Phone.

Key features of iOS 1:

  • Visual Voicemail​
  • Multitouch interface
  • Calculator
  • Calendar
  • Camera
  • Clock
  • iPod
  • iTunes
  • Mail
  • Maps
  • Music (iPod Touch)
  • Notes
  • Phone
  • Photos
  • Safari
  • Settings
  • Stocks
  • Text
  • Videos (iPod Touch)
  • Weather
  • YouTube

A Look Back—and Forward—at the History of iOS

From its humble beginnings as iPhone OS to the powerful and intelligent iOS 26, Apple’s mobile operating system has consistently led innovation in the smartphone world. Each update has not only refined the user experience but also anticipated what’s next in mobile technology.

As Apple moves forward with Apple Intelligence, spatial design, and deeper device integration, iOS continues to set the standard for what a modern mobile OS can achieve.

mainEntity.name: Will I lose my photos, apps, or purchases if I change my Apple ID email?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope! All your data, purchases, and subscriptions stay with your account—they’re not tied to the email address.

mainEntity.name: Can I merge two Apple IDs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Unfortunately, Apple doesn’t allow merging accounts. But you can use Family Sharing to share purchases and subscriptions.

mainEntity.name: Can I use more than one Apple ID on my device?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can use different Apple IDs for iCloud and the App Store, or set up multiple user accounts on a Mac.

mainEntity.name: How do I remove someone else’s Apple ID from my device?

acceptedAnswer.text: Just sign out in Settings > [your name] > Sign Out, and enter the account password when prompted.

mainEntity.name: What if I don’t get a verification code?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check your spam or junk folder, or try resending the code. Still stuck? Visit Apple’s official support page for more help.

title.rendered: Everything New in tvOS 26: Apple TV’s Big Redesign

content.rendered:
Apple unveiled tvOS 26 at WWDC 2025 alongside iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and watchOS. While it often flies under the radar compared to iOS or macOS, this year’s tvOS update is a surprisingly robust one—and it’s not just about the shiny new Liquid Glass redesign. Here’s everything new in tvOS 26, explained in simple, user-friendly terms.

Table of Contents
  • A New Look with Liquid Glass
  • Apple Music Sing Gets iPhone Karaoke Mode
  • Profiles Automatically Show Up on Wake
  • App Logins Linked to Apple Account
  • Apple TV App Gets Vertical Posters and Smarter Layout
  • A Redesigned Control Center
  • FaceTime Enhancements
  • Permanent AirPlay Speaker Option
  • Support for Dolby Atmos 9.1.6 and Passthrough Audio
  • New Aerial Screensavers from India
  • Smart Home Upgrades
  • Release Timeline and Compatibility

    A New Look with Liquid Glass

    Let’s start with the most noticeable change. Apple has brought its new Liquid Glass design to tvOS, just like it did with its other operating systems. The interface feels more modern and dynamic—buttons reflect light, menu bars subtly distort the background, and everything from the Control Center to the playback screens feels more immersive and alive.

    Important Note: Liquid Glass is only available on Apple TV 4K (2nd and 3rd generation) models. Older Apple TVs will continue using the previous flat design.

    Apple Music Sing Gets iPhone Karaoke Mode

    tvOS 26 levels up the karaoke experience. With Apple Music Sing, your iPhone now becomes a wireless mic. Just scan a QR code, and your phone turns into a mic—complete with a mute button and emoji reactions.

    When you sing, your voice plays directly through the TV speakers. You’ll also get:

    • Real-time lyrics on screen.
    • Live emoji cheers from friends.
    • Lyric translation and pronunciation tools, helping you sing in different languages.

    This feature works only on Apple TV 4K (3rd gen) and iPhone 11 or later.

    Profiles Automatically Show Up on Wake

    Apple TV now automatically displays user profiles when waking up. No more manual switching—you’re instantly taken to your personal watchlist, Apple Music playlists, and content recommendations. This makes Apple TV feel smarter and more tailored, especially in households with multiple users.

    App Logins Linked to Apple Account

    Setting up a new Apple TV just became easier. With tvOS 26, supported apps can now log in using your Apple ID. That means no more typing passwords for every streaming app. Developers can implement this via a new API, making the setup process faster and more secure.

    Apple TV App Gets Vertical Posters and Smarter Layout

    The Apple TV app is also getting a visual and functional refresh. Vertical poster art now replaces traditional wide banners, allowing you to view more content at once.

    Other improvements include:

    • Smarter Watchlist layout.
    • Labels showing streaming availability, episode duration, and “new” tags for fresh content.

    A Redesigned Control Center

    The Control Center gets the Liquid Glass upgrade too. It maintains the familiar four-tab layout (Profiles, Quick Controls, Apple Home, and VPN), but now features sleek visuals, soft reflections, and an immersive interface that matches the overall redesign.

    FaceTime Enhancements

    tvOS 26 improves the FaceTime experience on Apple TV. Here’s what’s new:

    • Notifications for incoming calls (video and audio).
    • Contact Posters that display a caller’s photo and name.
    • Expanded Live Captions support in multiple languages including:
      • French
      • German
      • Japanese
      • Korean
      • Mandarin
      • Spanish

    Permanent AirPlay Speaker Option

    Previously, only select HomePods could be set as the default speaker. With tvOS 26, you can now set any AirPlay-compatible speaker—including third-party speakers and soundbars—as the permanent audio output. Ideal for enhanced audio setups.

    Support for Dolby Atmos 9.1.6 and Passthrough Audio

    For audiophiles, tvOS 26 introduces support for Dolby Atmos 9.1.6. This adds two additional speaker channels—one in front and one above—for a richer surround sound experience.

    It also supports passthrough audio, which allows unprocessed sound to be sent directly to your AV receiver, ensuring pristine audio fidelity.

    New Aerial Screensavers from India

    Apple has added stunning new aerial screen savers from India, including scenic visuals from Goa and Kerala. For the first time, users can choose specific videos to display or hide, rather than disabling an entire screen saver category.

    Smart Home Upgrades

    tvOS 26 enhances Apple TV’s role as a Home Hub. It now supports Thread 1.4, which strengthens the mesh network between your smart devices. While this update didn’t introduce major new smart home features, it prepares Apple TV for better reliability with future Matter-compatible accessories.

    Release Timeline and Compatibility

    • Developer Beta: Available now
    • Public Beta: Arriving in July
    • Final Release: Scheduled for Fall 2025

    Compatibility: tvOS 26 works with all Apple TV 4K and Apple TV HD models, but advanced features like Liquid Glass and Karaoke Mic Mode require the latest hardware.

    A Surprisingly Big Year for Apple TV

    tvOS 26 may not grab headlines like iOS or macOS, but it delivers one of the most user-focused updates Apple TV has seen in years. From personalized profiles and karaoke fun to powerful audio upgrades and smart home readiness, Apple’s media hub is evolving—quietly, but confidently.

    Related articles worth reading:

    • Everything Apple Just Announced at WWDC 2025
    • Apple Intelligence Features Unveiled at WWDC 2025
    • Here’s Why Apple Skipped iOS 19 and Jumped Straight to iOS 26

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, it's generally safe, but not ideal for primary devices. Expect glitches, and some apps may not function properly.

mainEntity.name: Will I lose my photos, apps, or purchases if I change my Apple ID email?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope! All your data, purchases, and subscriptions stay with your account—they’re not tied to the email address.

mainEntity.name: Can I merge two Apple IDs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Unfortunately, Apple doesn’t allow merging accounts. But you can use Family Sharing to share purchases and subscriptions.

mainEntity.name: Can I use more than one Apple ID on my device?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can use different Apple IDs for iCloud and the App Store, or set up multiple user accounts on a Mac.

mainEntity.name: How do I remove someone else’s Apple ID from my device?

acceptedAnswer.text: Just sign out in Settings > [your name] > Sign Out, and enter the account password when prompted.

mainEntity.name: What if I don’t get a verification code?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check your spam or junk folder, or try resending the code. Still stuck? Visit Apple’s official support page for more help.

title.rendered: How to Use Apple Image Playground to Create AI Art on iPhone

content.rendered:
With the rise of AI image generators, Apple has launched its own take, Image Playground. As part of Apple Intelligence, this new app lets you generate playful and original AI art in just a few taps. From creating Genmoji to personal avatars, Image Playground makes AI fun, secure, and fully integrated into your Apple ecosystem.

Keep reading to learn how to use Apple Image Playground on iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

Table of Contents
  • What is Image Playground on iPhone and iPad?
  • Which Devices Support Apple Image Playground?
  • How to Use Image Playground on iPhone and iPad
    • Use Apple's Suggestions
    • Generate AI Images Using Descriptions
    • Create AI Avatars with the People Album
    • Generate Images from Photos
    • Change Image Styles
    • Use ChatGPT Styles for More Variety
    • Create Genmoji
    • How to Share AI Images from Image Playground
  • How to Use Image Playground in the Messages App
  • How to Use Image Playground in the Notes App
  • Fix: ‘Downloading Support for Image Playground' Stuck?
  • Watch: How to Use Image Playground in iOS 18.2

What is Image Playground on iPhone and iPad?

Introduced in iOS 18.2 and enhanced in iOS 26, Image Playground is a built-in app that lets you create AI-generated images using descriptions, Apple’s suggestions, or photos from your gallery. You can also use it inside native Apple apps like Messages and Notes.

Unlike many other AI tools, Image Playground only generates cartoon-like images, avoiding photorealistic results to prevent the spread of misinformation. The best part? All image generation occurs on-device, ensuring your data remains private and secure.

Which Devices Support Apple Image Playground?

Since it’s part of Apple Intelligence, Image Playground only works on compatible devices running:

  • iOS 18.2 or later
  • iPadOS 18.2 or later
  • macOS Sequoia 15.2 or later

To see if your device supports it, check our dedicated guide on Apple Intelligence-supported models and learn how to fix issues if Image Playground is not working.

How to Use Image Playground on iPhone and iPad

Once your device is updated, the Image Playground app will appear on your Home Screen (iPhone/iPad) or Dock (Mac). Open it, and you’re ready to start creating.

1. Use Apple’s Suggestions

Here’s how you can use Apple Suggestions to refine images in the Image Playground app:

  1. Open the Image Playground app, and you will see the Suggestions bar at the bottom.
  2. Use one from the currently visible suggestions or tap the Show More button to reveal suggestions based on themes such as Fireworks, Birthday, Halloween, Party, Sci-Fi, Adventure, Disco, and more.

  3. Swipe left on the theme suggestions to reveal more, and you will see costume suggestions for Artist, Chef, Astronaut, and more.
  4. The next left swipe will reveal accessories suggestions, like Beanie, Sunglasses, Bow Tie, and several others.
  5. With another left swipe, Image Playground lets you choose from various places, including City, Forest, Stage, and more.

Generate AI Images Using Descriptions

Like any other AI image generator, Image Playground also lets you generate AI images using the descriptions you provide. You can type anything, and the corresponding image will be generated. You can also add more to the description or modify it to refine the final image.

Here’s how you can do this:

  1. Open the Image Playground app and type any word or phrase you want in the Describe an Image text box at the bottom. Image Playground will automatically start figuring out the image based on your typing.
  2. Once you finish writing the description, hit the Done button, and the app will create the corresponding images for it.

  3. You can also modify the image using Apple suggestions, existing photos or additional word descriptions. Image Playground will refine the result to acclimate to the changes as you make them.
  4. The app will create a set of four images based on the given description. You can swipe through them and select the one you like.
  5. Once you select the image, tap the Done button to save the image in the app.

Create AI Avatars with the People Album

Here’s how you can create AI avatars in the Image Playground app:

  1. In the Image Playground app, tap the Person button next to the description field.
  2. Here, choose the person whose AI avatar you want to create. You can also choose appearance and use the built-in options to create an avatar.
  3. If the person is selected for the first time, you are asked to choose a starting point. The app will display different renderings based on photos of the same person in your photo library. Once selected, the Image Playground app will generate the person’s AI avatar in a matter of seconds.

  4. You can also add a description or use Apple’s suggestion to make the AI avatar more fun.
  5. Once the Image is generated, swipe on it to view the options and tap the Done button when you feel content with how it looks.

Generate Images from Photos

To create art from a photo:

  1. Tap the + button in the bottom-right corner.
  2. If you wish to use an existing image, tap Choose Photo. Otherwise, tap Take Photo to take a new photo using the built-in camera.

  3. Once the photo is selected, the Image Playground app will quickly generate up to four AI images using it. Swipe through generated images, select the one you like, and tap Done.

Change Image Styles

Apple offers three image styles. Here’s how you choose between the three style options:

  1. Tap the Style button at the top center.
  2. Now, choose between the Animation, Illustration, and Sketch style options.

You can easily view the difference each style has on the generated image.

Use ChatGPT Styles for More Variety

With iOS 26, Apple added ChatGPT integration for a more artistic style. The output is similar to what you get if you use ChatGPT 4o for image generation, and you can even generate realistic images, which is not something that Apple’s image generation technology does.

Here’s how you can choose between ChatGPT styles:

  1. Tap the Style button at the top center.
  2. Now, select the ChatGPT style option.
  3. Next, select the desired image style under the ChatGPT style section.
  4. You can choose the Any Style option if you don’t want to restrict image generation to use a specific style.
  5. Once done, use a text prompt, a custom image, Apple’s suggestions, or a combination of all to generate ChatGPT-style AI images.

Users with a free ChatGPT account can only generate one or two images per day. However, users with premium accounts can utilize tokens to generate additional images.

Create Genmoji

Initially launched in Messages, Genmoji is now available in Image Playground.

To create one:

  1. Tap the Style button at the top center and select Genmoji.
  2. Now, choose one or multiple emojis from the Suggestions bar to create a new Genmoji. You can also add a text description along with emojis to create a new Genmoji.

How to Share AI Images from Image Playground

Once the AI image is generated and you are satisfied with it, you can share it via multiple means or save it to share later.

  1. Tap the Done button in the top-right corner.
  2. Next, tap the Share button in the bottom-left corner and select one of the various available options in the Share Sheet.

  3. To share previously created images, open the Image Playground app. The first screen will be the gallery with all the previously generated images. Select the desired image and tap the Share button to access the Share Sheet and pick an app.

Note: Shared images are labeled as “generated image” in iOS 26.

How to Use Image Playground in the Messages App

Apple embedded Image Playground right inside Messages for quick sharing.

To use it:

  1. Open the Messages app and head to an existing conversation thread or create a new one.
  2. Here, tap the + button before the text field at the bottom.
  3. Next, choose the Image Playground option in the menu that appears.

  4. This will open a mini version of the original Image Playground app within the Messages app. Use Apple’s suggestion, give an image description, or other available options to create an AI image.
  5. Once the image is generated, tap on Done, then hit the send button (with an upward-pointing arrow) in the bottom-right corner.

Apple may even suggest contextual image ideas based on your conversation!

How to Use Image Playground in the Notes App

In the Notes app, Image Playground is accessed via the Image Wand in the Apple Pencil palette.

  1. Draw a rough shape or circle
  2. Image Wand reads the surrounding content
  3. It auto-generates an AI image to match your context
  4. Add it directly to your Note for more engaging visuals

This feature also works in Freeform and Keynote.

Fix: ‘Downloading Support for Image Playground’ Stuck?

If your app gets stuck:

  • Wait It Out: Apple may be rolling out access in waves to prevent server overload
  • Check Apple Intelligence Settings:
    • Go to Settings → Apple Intelligence & Siri
    • Ensure Apple Intelligence is toggled ON

Watch: How to Use Image Playground in iOS 18.2

Start Creating AI Art with Image Playground Today

That’s everything you need to know about Apple Image Playground—the easiest way to create AI art on iPhone, iPad, and Mac. With deep integration into Apple apps and privacy-first processing, it’s a fun and safe way to express your creativity.

Have you tried it yet? Share your favorite AI image in the comments!

Also read:

  • How to use Apple Intelligence in the Mail app on an iPhone
  • How to summarize webpages in Safari using Apple Intelligence
  • How to use writing tools with Apple Intelligence on iPhone
  • How to Use Perplexity AI to Generate Images on WhatsApp

title.rendered: iPhone 16 Charger Type: What to Use and How to Choose

content.rendered:
Quick Takeaways
  • The iPhone 16 uses USB-C for charging and data transfer.
  • A 20W USB-C adapter is the minimum for fast charging (0–50% in about 30 minutes).
  • Higher-wattage (30W–100W+) chargers are safe, future-proof, and ideal for power users or multi-device households.
  • Cable quality matters—always use certified, high-speed USB-C cables.
  • MagSafe wireless charging offers the fastest wireless experience (up to 15–20W).
  • Choose your charger based on your daily habits, travel needs, and device ecosystem.
  • Smart charging habits and iOS features can significantly extend your battery’s lifespan.

Choosing the right charger for your iPhone 16 is about more than just plugging in—it’s about getting the most out of your device in a way that fits your daily routine. Whether you’re a busy professional, a frequent traveler, or someone who just wants to keep things simple at home, I’m here to walk you through everything you need to know.

In this guide, you’ll find clear explanations of iPhone 16 charger types, power ratings, and real-world charging speeds, all tailored to help you pick the perfect option for your lifestyle. I’ll also share practical tips for keeping your battery healthy, so your iPhone 16 stays powerful and ready whenever you need it.

The Transition to USB-C: Why It Matters

Apple began using USB-C as the main charging and data port for iPhones with the iPhone 15. The iPhone 16 also uses USB-C, offering several advantages:

  1. Universal compatibility: Works seamlessly with modern laptops, tablets, and accessories—no more juggling multiple cables.
  2. Faster charging and data transfer: Supports higher power delivery and speedier data transfers.
  3. Environmental benefits: Standardizing USB-C reduces cable waste and supports Apple’s sustainability goals.
  4. Convenience: One port and cable for all your Apple devices and many third-party products.
Note: The iPhone 16 comes with just a USB-C cable in the box. You will need a USB-C power adapter or a wireless charger to use it.

What Type of Charger Does iPhone 16 Use?

The iPhone 16 uses a USB-C port for charging and transferring data, instead of the old Lightning connector. This common standard makes charging easier and faster, which is excellent for modern devices.

To ensure full compatibility and optimal performance:

  1. Use a USB-C power adapter that supports USB Power Delivery (USB-PD).
  2. For wireless charging, choose a MagSafe or Qi-compatible charger.

Wired Charging Standards & Wattage

  • 20W USB-C Adapter: The baseline for fast charging. It delivers up to 50% charge in about 30 minutes, which is suitable for most users.
  • 30W–40W Chargers: Provide a slight speed boost, especially helpful if you multitask, game, or need quick top-ups.
  • 65W–100W+ Multi-Port Chargers: Ideal for charging your iPhone, iPad, MacBook, and more from a single outlet—perfect for power users, families, and travel.

Charging Times (Typical):

  • 20W: 0–50% in 30 min | Full charge in ~2 hours
  • 30–40W: 0–50% in 25 min | Full charge in ~1.7 hours
  • 65W+: 0–50% in 20–25 min* | Full charge in ~1.5–1.7 hours

The actual charging time depends on your device and charger; iPhone 16 adjusts charging speed to protect the battery.

Pro Tip: Chargers with more power are safe to use—your iPhone will only use the amount it needs. Using a more powerful adapter also gets your charging setup ready for future devices.

Cable Quality: Don’t Overlook This Essential

A powerful charger is only as good as your cable. For best results:

  1. Use USB-C cables rated for USB 3.1 or higher (especially for fast charging and data transfer).
  2. Avoid cheap or uncertified cables—they may bottleneck charging speed or cause safety risks.

Recommended iPhone 16 Chargers

Everyday Use:

  1. Apple 20W USB-C Power Adapter
  2. Anker 20W USB-C Charging Block

Faster Charging & Multi-Device:

  1. UGREEN 35W USB-C Charger
  2. Belkin 65W Dual USB-C Charger
  3. Spigen 35W USB-C Charger

Ultimate Flexibility and Power:

  1. Anker 737 GaNPrime 120W (multi-port, laptop/tablet/phone)
  2. MacBook USB-C charger (great for iPhone 16 Pro models)

Wireless Charging: MagSafe and Qi Explained

  1. MagSafe: Apple’s magnetic wireless charging standard, offering up to 15–20W charging (model-dependent) with perfect alignment for maximum efficiency.
  2. Qi Wireless Pads: Universal, but typically slower (up to 7.5W). Still a good option for convenience, but not as fast as MagSafe.
Note: For the fastest wireless charging, always choose MagSafe-certified chargers.

Top Picks:

  1. Apple MagSafe Charger
  2. Anker MagGo Wireless Charger
  3. Spigen Wireless Charging Stand

How to Choose the Best Charger for Your Lifestyle

  1. Home/Office User: 20W–35W single-port charger is efficient and affordable.
  2. Power User/Traveler: 35W–100W multi-port GaN charger covers your phone, tablet, and laptop—one charger for all.
  3. Family/Shared Spaces: Multi-port (65W+) chargers minimize clutter and maximize convenience for households with multiple devices.
  4. On-the-Go: Compact MagSafe power banks or portable power stations keep you charged anywhere, even off-grid.
  5. Future-Proofing: Investing in a higher-wattage, multi-port charger now means you’re ready for future devices and charging needs—saving money and reducing e-waste.

Evaluating Charger Compatibility

When selecting a charger, consider:

  1. Wattage: At least 20W for fast charging; higher is better for multi-device use.
  2. Certification: Look for USB-PD compliance and reputable brands.
  3. Cable Quality: Use high-speed, certified USB-C cables.
  4. Device Ecosystem: Consider what other devices you’ll charge—laptops, tablets, headphones—to choose the correct wattage and number of ports.
  5. Wireless Support: Pick MagSafe for faster speeds or Qi for broad compatibility with wireless charging.

Can I Use My Older iPhone Charger?

  1. USB-A Adapters: You can use an old USB-A adapter with a USB-A to USB-C cable, but charging will be slower and may not support fast charging.
  2. For best results: Upgrade to a 20W or higher USB-C charger.

Unlocking Charger Versatility: Beyond Charging Your iPhone

Switching to USB-C is not only about faster charging—it also makes your iPhone 16 charger and cable more useful in new ways:

  1. Charge Other Devices: Power AirPods, Apple Watch (with the right cable), Bluetooth speakers, or portable game consoles.
  2. Connect to External Accessories: Use USB-C to HDMI/DisplayPort adapters for presentations, external storage for file transfer, or USB-C headphones for high-quality audio.
  3. Power Small Accessories: From portable fans to LED lights, one charger covers many needs.
  4. Boost Productivity: Use high-speed data transfer for backups, large file moves, or as a camera for your computer.
  5. Sustainability: USB-C’s universality means fewer cables and chargers, supporting a minimalist, eco-friendly lifestyle.
Tip: Not all accessories work the same way. Some need USB 3.1 or newer to work fully. Always check if they are compatible and use good quality cables.

Battery Life and Charging Optimization: Expert Strategies

Your iPhone 16’s battery lasts longer if you do more than just use the right charger. Here are some tips to help your battery stay healthy for a long time:

  1. Enable Optimized Battery Charging: Activate this setting (Settings > Battery > Battery Health & Charging) to reduce battery aging.
  2. Use Low Power Mode: Reduce background activity when you’re away from outlets or need to stretch your battery.
  3. Adjust Screen Brightness and Display Settings: Lower brightness, use Dark Mode and enable “Reduce Motion” to cut battery drain.
  4. Manage Background App Refresh and Location Services: Limit background app activity and location tracking for apps that don’t need them.
  5. Keep iOS Updated: Regular updates include performance and battery optimizations.
  6. Avoid Extreme Temperatures: Keep your iPhone between 32°–95°F (0°–35°C), and avoid leaving it in hot cars or direct sunlight while charging.
  7. Practice Smart Charging Habits: Use certified chargers and cables, charge in cool areas, avoid intensive use while charging, and unplug when fully charged.
  8. Monitor Battery Health: Check your battery’s maximum capacity in Settings and consider replacement if it drops below 80%.
  9. Personalize with Automation: Use Apple Shortcuts or Focus Modes to automate battery-saving actions.
  10. Bust Battery Myths: No need to fully drain your battery before recharging, and overnight charging is safe thanks to modern battery management.
Tip: Smarter charging is not only convenient—it also helps the environment. A longer-lasting battery means you create less electronic waste.

Choosing the Right Charger for Your iPhone 16

The iPhone 16 now uses USB-C, which means you can charge it faster, use it with more devices, and make your tech setup easier. Pick a USB-C adapter with 20W or more for daily use, or choose a stronger, multi-port charger if you want to charge several devices and be ready for the future. Remember to use good quality cables, charge your phone smartly, and use iOS features to keep your battery healthy and safe.

If you learn how you charge your phone and take better care of the battery, your iPhone 16 and other devices will work better for you.

FAQs

Does the iPhone 16 come with a charger in the box?

No, only a USB-C cable is included. You’ll need to purchase a compatible adapter or use a wireless charger.

Will a higher-wattage charger damage my iPhone?

No—your iPhone only draws the power it needs. Higher-wattage adapters are safe and can be used for other devices.

Does cable quality really matter?

Yes. Use certified USB-C cables rated for high-speed power delivery for fast charging and safe operation.

Can I use my MacBook charger for my iPhone 16?

Absolutely! It’s a great way to reduce the number of chargers you need.

  • iPhone 16 vs. iPhone 15: Which iPhone is best for you?
  • What does “Slow Charger” mean on iPhone, and how to fix it
  • Is the iPhone 16 or 16 Pro waterproof? What you need to know
  • Best cases for iPhone 16 and iPhone 16 Pro

mainEntity.name: Can I merge two Apple IDs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Unfortunately, Apple doesn’t allow merging accounts. But you can use Family Sharing to share purchases and subscriptions.

mainEntity.name: Can I use more than one Apple ID on my device?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can use different Apple IDs for iCloud and the App Store, or set up multiple user accounts on a Mac.

mainEntity.name: How do I remove someone else’s Apple ID from my device?

acceptedAnswer.text: Just sign out in Settings > [your name] > Sign Out, and enter the account password when prompted.

mainEntity.name: What if I don’t get a verification code?

title.rendered: Spotify on Apple Watch: Stream, Download & Control Music Anytime, Anywhere

content.rendered:
Heading out for a morning run and don’t want to take your iPhone, but still want to enjoy your favorite tracks? Spotify on Apple Watch has your back.

Spotify on Apple Watch is one of the most convenient ways to listen to music and podcasts—even when your paired iPhone isn’t nearby. From controlling playback and downloading for offline use to streaming music directly, it brings your favorite tunes right to your wrist.

Here’s everything you need to know to get the most out of Spotify on Apple Watch.

Why Use Spotify on Apple Watch?

With Apple Music integrated seamlessly into the Apple ecosystem, you might wonder, “Why use Spotify at all?” Here’s why millions prefer Spotify—even on their Apple Watch:

  • Personalized Playlists: Spotify’s discovery algorithm is top-tier. From Daily Mixes to Release Radar, Spotify often nails your vibe better than Apple Music.
  • Free Tier Available: Unlike Apple Music, Spotify offers a free version (with ads), allowing more users to enjoy it without a subscription.
  • Spotify Connect: Control playback on any Spotify-connected device—like smart speakers, consoles, or desktops—right from your wrist.

Related: Apple Music vs. Spotify: Which is the best music streaming platform?

Prerequisites to Use Spotify on Apple Watch

Before diving in, make sure your setup checks all the boxes:

  • Apple Watch Series 3 or later running watchOS 7 or newer.
  • Spotify app installed on your paired iPhone.
  • An active Spotify account (Premium required for streaming or downloads).
  • Bluetooth headphones or AirPods paired with your Apple Watch.
  • Spotify app installed on the Apple Watch: Open the Watch app on iPhone → Tap My Watch → Scroll to Available Apps → Tap Install next to Spotify.

How to Stream Music and Podcasts From Your Apple Watch

If you’re a Spotify Premium subscriber, you can stream music directly on your Apple Watch. Here’s how:

Note For streaming, your Apple Watch must be connected to Wi-Fi or have cellular service enabled.
  1. Open the Spotify app on your Apple Watch.
  2. Swipe right on the player screen to browse and play a track from your library.
  3. If the track you want to listen to isn’t in your library, swipe left on the player screen and tap the Magnifying Glass (Search) button to search for the intended track or podcast.
  4. Tap the song name to play it and connect your Bluetooth headphones if they’re not already paired.

How to Download Playlists and Podcasts for Offline Playback

Spotify Premium users can download audio to their Apple Watch for offline listening—ideal for flights, gyms, or no-signal zones.

To download directly from your Apple Watch:

  1. Make sure your Apple Watch is connected to the internet.
  2. Open the Spotify app and navigate to the playlist, album, or podcast you’d like to download.
  3. Tap the Download (Downward arrow in a circle) button and wait for the download to complete.

To queue downloads from iPhone, iPad, or Mac:

Even if your Apple Watch isn’t on your wrist, you can still queue downloads:

  1. Open the Spotify app on the paired iPhone.
  2. Navigate to the playlist or podcast you want to download on your Apple Watch.
  3. Tap the three-dot (more options) button.
  4. Select the “Download to other devices” option in the pop-up menu.
  5. Tap the Download button next to the Apple Watch.

Your Watch will start downloading the files automatically when it’s charging and connected to Wi‑Fi.

Use Siri and Watch Face Complications for Quick Access

Control Spotify without touching the screen:

Say:

“Hey Siri, play [artist or playlist name] on Spotify”

Want even faster access? Add Spotify to your Watch face:

  1. Tap the hold the watch face with complications and tap the Edit button.
  2. Swipe right to access Complications and select the Complication you want to replace the Spotify complication with.
  3. Tap the Back button at the top right corner.
  4. Locate and select the Spotify app.
  5. Select the Spotify Complication to add it to the watch face.

Now, just tap the Spotify complication to open the app instantly.

Troubleshooting Common Spotify Issues on Apple Watch

Run into a hiccup? Try these quick fixes:

Ready to Listen on the Go?

Spotify turns your Apple Watch into a mini music hub—perfect for runs, workouts, commutes, or simply disconnecting from your iPhone. With streaming, offline playback, Siri support, and watch face complications, you’ve got everything you need—right on your wrist.

Got any tips or questions about Spotify on Apple Watch? Share them in the comments below!

  • Apple Music Now Lets You Transfer Playlists from Spotify and Other Services

mainEntity.name: Will I lose my photos, apps, or purchases if I change my Apple ID email?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope! All your data, purchases, and subscriptions stay with your account—they’re not tied to the email address.

mainEntity.name: Can I merge two Apple IDs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Unfortunately, Apple doesn’t allow merging accounts. But you can use Family Sharing to share purchases and subscriptions.

mainEntity.name: Can I use more than one Apple ID on my device?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can use different Apple IDs for iCloud and the App Store, or set up multiple user accounts on a Mac.

mainEntity.name: How do I remove someone else’s Apple ID from my device?

acceptedAnswer.text: Just sign out in Settings > [your name] > Sign Out, and enter the account password when prompted.

mainEntity.name: What if I don’t get a verification code?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check your spam or junk folder, or try resending the code. Still stuck? Visit Apple’s official support page for more help.

acceptedAnswer.text: No, only a USB-C cable is included. You'll need to purchase a compatible adapter or use a wireless charger.

title.rendered: Apple Joins China’s Subsidy Program to Boost iPhone, Mac Sales

content.rendered:
In a move to combat declining sales in China, Apple has joined China’s national digital product subsidy program through its direct sales channels, according to the South China Morning Post. This will allow eligible customers in Beijing and Shanghai to receive government-backed discounts on select iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple Watch models.

How the Subsidy Program Works

The program offers a discount of up to 2,000 yuan (approximately $278) on select Apple products, with the device’s price determining eligibility.

Products priced under 6,000 yuan ($835) receive a 15% discount capped at 500 yuan ($70), while higher-value items, like Macs, qualify for larger subsidies.

In Shanghai, customers can benefit from this subsidy by buying an eligible device from one of the eight Apple Stores. Beijing residents, on the other hand, can receive the discount via Apple’s Online Store as long as they use a Beijing shipping address.

First-Time Direct Participation by Apple

This isn’t the first time Apple products have been available under the program. Previously, they were offered only through authorized third-party platforms such as JD.com and Alibaba’s Taobao. However, Apple’s own retail and online stores are now participating directly.

A Response to Declining Shipments

This initiative comes as Apple seeks to revitalize its sales in China, where iPhone sales have declined notably in 2025. Market analysts note that Apple is the only top-five smartphone vendor to see a drop in shipments this year, while rivals like Xiaomi and Huawei have experienced significant growth.

iGeeksBlog Take

As China remains a vital market—and with competitors like Xiaomi and Huawei making aggressive gains—Apple’s direct participation in the program appears both timely and strategic. This can help the Cupertino tech giant reverse its sales slump. Given its premium image, Apple rarely joins such programs, so this is a significant and telling shift in its China strategy.

What’s your take on Apple joining China’s subsidy program? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below.

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope! All your data, purchases, and subscriptions stay with your account—they’re not tied to the email address.

acceptedAnswer.text: Unfortunately, Apple doesn’t allow merging accounts. But you can use Family Sharing to share purchases and subscriptions.

mainEntity.name: Can I use more than one Apple ID on my device?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can use different Apple IDs for iCloud and the App Store, or set up multiple user accounts on a Mac.

acceptedAnswer.text: Just sign out in Settings > [your name] > Sign Out, and enter the account password when prompted.

title.rendered: Apple Wallet F1 Ad Draws Backlash from iPhone Users

content.rendered:
Apple just pushed the wrong button—literally. This week, the tech giant sent out a push notification through the Wallet app, promoting a $10 Apple Pay discount on two tickets for its upcoming movie F1. What might’ve seemed like harmless marketing to some triggered frustration and distrust among many iPhone users.

A Promo in the Wrong Place?

The notification was part of a partnership with Fandango, offering users a discount when they paid with Apple Pay. On the surface, it’s a harmless promo. However, what caused the stir was where and how Apple chose to deliver it: through the Wallet app, a system-level app that handles sensitive financial tasks, such as storing credit cards, boarding passes, and concert tickets.

For a lot of people, that’s sacred ground. Users took to X, Reddit, and tech forums to air their disappointment. One person posted, “I didn’t drop $1,000+ on an iPhone to get ads from my Wallet app.” Others likened it to a breach of trust, calling it an invasive move that blurs the line between utility and promotion.

Is Apple Breaking Its Own Rules?

It’s not just about discomfort—it might be a direct contradiction of Apple’s own policies. According to Apple’s App Review Guidelines (section 4.5.4), push notifications shouldn’t be used for promotions unless the user explicitly opts in and has an easy opt-out option.

However, in this case, users received the Wallet promo without their consent, and those running iOS 18 found that they couldn’t disable promotions without also shutting off all Wallet notifications. That’s not a viable tradeoff for most.

Interestingly, iOS 26 beta introduces a new toggle in Wallet settings under Notifications labeled “Offers & Promotions.” It allows users to opt out of such promotional content, but this feature is currently only available to developers and beta testers.

The “F1 Push” Is Reminding Users of a Past Mistake

The incident is already drawing comparisons to the infamous U2 album fiasco of 2014, when Apple forced-installed a U2 album onto users’ libraries without consent. That move led to widespread backlash and a rare public apology. Some are now calling this Apple’s “F1 Push” moment of 2025.

Users Divided—But It’s Not Just About $10

Defenders of Apple argue this is overblown. Since Wallet already manages tickets and entertainment, promoting a movie deal might not seem out of place. And hey—$10 off is still a win, right?

However, critics argue that the real concern isn’t the discount, but rather the precedent. If Apple begins treating system apps like marketing channels, what’s next? Ads in Settings? Promos through Health?

It all boils down to trust—something Apple markets heavily with its privacy-first positioning. When a platform like Wallet, built around personal security and discretion, starts pushing ads, it raises red flags for users who expect more from a premium device.

A Slippery Slope for System App Ads?

In an era where digital advertising feels unavoidable, Apple has long stood apart by prioritizing user control and clean, ad-free system experiences. This move signals a shift, and for many, even one push notification was one too many.

If Apple doesn’t course correct, the fear is that this might just be the beginning of a new, more intrusive chapter in how it communicates with users.

title.rendered: Can You See Who Viewed Your Instagram Profile? Find Out Now

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways
  • No. You can’t see who looks at your Instagram profile—no exceptions.
  • You’ll only see who watched your Stories (for 48 hours) or joined your Live video (while it’s happening).
  • Apps that promise to show you profile viewers? They’re scams and can put your account at risk.
  • Instagram gives you privacy tools—use them to control who sees your stuff.
  • If someone makes you uncomfortable, use restrict, block, or report. Instagram keeps these actions private.

You’re not the only one! With so many people using Instagram, it’s totally normal to be curious about who’s visiting your profile. Maybe you’re hoping for a secret admirer, or maybe you just want to know if someone’s “stalking” you. So, does Instagram show who viewed your profile?

Let’s clear up the confusion. This guide breaks down what Instagram actually shows you, what stays private, why those “profile viewer” apps are a bad idea, and how you can stay safe and in control.

Table of Contents
  • Can You See Who Views Your Profile on Instagram
  • What Can You Actually See on Instagram?
  • Instagram vs. Other Social Platforms
  • Why Does Instagram Keep Profile Views Private?
  • What Activity Can You See on Instagram?
  • Instagram Business Accounts and Analytics
    • Instagram Insights lets you track:
    • How to Access Instagram Insights:
    • What Can You See About Post Engagement?
  • Common Myths, Scams, and Misconceptions
  • Third-Party Apps: Risks and Reality
  • How to Protect Your Privacy on Instagram
    • How to block someone:
    • Manage Story and Post Visibility
    • If You Feel Unsafe or Harassed
  • The Role of Instagram's Algorithm
  • Ethical and Social Considerations
  • The Truth About Instagram Profile Views

Can You See Who Views Your Profile on Instagram

Short answer: Nope! Instagram does not let anyone see who’s checked out their profile. This is true for everyone—personal, creator, or business accounts, and on any device. Instagram keeps profile browsing totally anonymous.

For example: LinkedIn sometimes tells you when someone views your profile. Instagram? It never does.

What Can You Actually See on Instagram?

Instagram treats every feature a little differently. Here’s how it works:

  1. Profile: You can’t see who visits, ever.
  2. Stories: You can see who watched your Story, but only for 48 hours after you post it.
  3. Highlights: Once a Story becomes a Highlight, the viewer info disappears.
  4. Reels and Feed Posts: You’ll see who liked, commented, or shared—but not who just viewed.
  5. Profile Picture: No one can see if you viewed their profile photo.
  6. Live Video: If you go live, you’ll see who’s watching in real time, but that list goes away when the live ends.

Instagram vs. Other Social Platforms

How does Instagram’s privacy approach compare to other major social platforms?

Insight: Instagram is stricter than most platforms about profile view privacy, letting users explore content freely without exposing their browsing activity.

Why Does Instagram Keep Profile Views Private?

Instagram’s goal is to let you browse and discover new accounts without feeling watched or judged. Keeping profile views private means you can explore freely—no pressure, no drama.

What Activity Can You See on Instagram?

While profile views are always private, you can see who interacts with your content in specific ways:

Instagram Stories

  1. When you post a Story, you can view a list of who’s watched it by swiping it up while it’s active.
  2. Viewer list is available for up to 48 hours after posting.
  3. The order of viewers is influenced by your interactions and Instagram’s algorithm—it’s not strictly chronological or a sign of “stalking.”

Example: If you post a Story at 10 am, you can check the viewer list until 10 am two days later. After that, the viewer data disappears.

Instagram Business Accounts and Analytics

Business or creator accounts get access to Instagram Insights. While you still can’t see individual profile. viewers, you’ll get useful aggregated data to help grow your presence.

Instagram Insights lets you track:

  1. Profile visits: Total number of times your profile was viewed in a given period.
  2. Follower growth: How many followers you gained or lost over time.
  3. Impressions and reach: How often your content was seen and by how many unique accounts.
  4. Audience demographics: Age, gender, top locations, and when your followers are most active.
  5. Content performance: Engagement metrics for each post, Story, Reel, or Live.
  6. Website and action button clicks: Number of users who clicked your bio link, called, emailed, or requested directions.

How to Access Instagram Insights:

  1. Switch to a Professional Account (Business or Creator) under Settings > Account.
  2. Post content and allow at least 7 days for data to start populating.
  3. Tap “Insights” on your profile or view analytics for individual posts and Stories.

Important: Instagram Insights only shows aggregate numbers and trends. You’ll never see a list of individual profile visitors.

Example: You might learn that your profile had 200 visits last week, but you won’t know who those visitors were.

What Can You See About Post Engagement?

You can always see:

  1. Who liked, commented on, or shared your posts.
  2. Who viewed your Stories (for a limited time).

If someone just looks at your profile or scrolls through your posts without interacting, you won’t be notified or see their username.

Common Myths, Scams, and Misconceptions

You might see lots of “hacks” or myths online about seeing your profile viewers. Here’s what’s really true:

  • “Turning your account public for a day lets you see profile viewers.”
  • False—Instagram never displays profile viewers, regardless of your account type.
  • “Using certain hashtags or third-party apps will show your stalkers.”
  • False—Instagram’s official policy and API make this impossible.
  • “If someone always watches your Stories, they’re stalking your profile.”
  • Not necessarily—Story views only show who watched your Story, not who visited your profile.

Third-Party Apps: Risks and Reality

No app or service can show you who viewed your Instagram profile. Apps that claim to do so are scams and pose serious security risks:

  1. They often require your Instagram login, which can lead to hacking or data theft.
  2. Many install malware or steal personal information.
  3. Using unauthorized apps can result in your account being suspended or banned.

Instagram’s Stance: Instagram’s terms of service prohibit the collection of profile view data by third parties, and the platform actively works to prevent unauthorized data access.

How to Protect Your Privacy on Instagram

Want more privacy or control? Here’s how to manage who sees your content and interacts with you:

Make Your Account Private

  1. Go to your Instagram profile and tap the three lines in the corner.
  2. Select “Settings and privacy”.
  3. Tap “Account privacy”.
  4. Toggle on “Private account”.

Result: Only people you approve as followers can see your posts and Stories.

Restrict or Block Users

  1. Restrict: Limits what a user can see and do on your profile without notifying them.
  2. Block: Prevents the user from entirely seeing your profile, posts, or Stories.

Related: What happens when you restrict someone on Instagram?

How to block someone:

  1. Visit their Instagram profile.
  2. Tap the three dots in the top right.
  3. Select “Block”.

Manage Story and Post Visibility

  1. Hide Stories from specific users.
  2. Create a Close Friends list for more privacy.

Example: If you want only close friends to see certain Stories, add them to your Close Friends list before posting.

If You Feel Unsafe or Harassed

  1. Restrict or block the user to limit their access to your content.
  2. Make your account private so only approved followers see your posts.
  3. Report harassment using Instagram’s reporting tools.

Note: Instagram keeps these actions private, so blocked users are not notified.

The Role of Instagram’s Algorithm

Sometimes, Instagram’s algorithm might put your content on the Explore page or suggest it to new people. That means more profile visits from strangers—but you’ll never know who they are, and neither will anyone else.

Ethical and Social Considerations

If Instagram revealed profile viewers, would you feel comfortable browsing? There’s a balance between transparency and privacy. While some users want more information, others value anonymity and the freedom to explore profiles without judgment. Instagram’s approach is designed to protect both sides.

In some cultures, browsing profiles openly is normal; in others, privacy is highly valued. Instagram’s privacy tools help users tailor their experience to their own comfort level.

The Truth About Instagram Profile Views

Instagram is all about sharing, connecting, and exploring without worrying about who’s watching. Use the privacy tools, stay smart about your information, and enjoy your time on the app!

Do you want to adjust the tone or explore a specific topic? Let me know—I’m here to help!

FAQs

Can someone see how many times you view their profile?

No—Instagram never shares this information. You can visit any profile as often as you want without the other person knowing.

Can business or creator accounts see who viewed their profile?

No. Professional accounts can only see the total number of profile visits and general demographic data—not specific visitors.

Are there any legitimate apps to check profile viewers?

No. Any app or service claiming to reveal your Instagram profile viewers is misleading and potentially dangerous.

Can someone see if you viewed their Instagram profile picture?

No. Viewing someone’s profile picture does not trigger any notification, and there is no way for users to see who has viewed their profile photo.

Can you see who viewed your Instagram Highlights?

No. Highlights are made up of Stories, but once a Story becomes a Highlight, you can no longer see who viewed it.

For more Instagram tips and tricks:

  • How to hide your active status on Instagram
  • How to make and use Instagram Avatar on iPhone
  • Change your Instagram password or reset it
  • How to See Watch History on Instagram
